fluff.overview:
The Burrock is a 75-ton Clan heavy BattleMech introduced in 3066 by Clan Star Adder. Named for the Eden burrock, a large subterranean invertebrate known for boring through solid rock, the design was developed as a dedicated close-range brawler following the politically complex absorption of Clan Burrock. The 'Mech was conceived as both a combat platform and a symbol of respect for the absorbed Clan's heritage, intended to earn the loyalty of former Burrock warriors through recognition rather than forced assimilation.

Built at the Albion Armor Works facility, the Burrock fills a short-range assault role in the Star Adder touman. Its reputation as a relentless close-quarters combatant reflects both its devastating firepower at point-blank range and the fierce pride of the warriors who pilot it.
fluff.capabilities:
At 75 tons, the Burrock sits at the top of the heavy weight class and moves fast enough to keep pace with most Clan 'Mechs, achieving a maximum speed of 86 kilometers per hour courtesy of a Modified 375-rated extra-light fusion engine. The XL engine does leave the 'Mech vulnerable to torso hits, but roughly twelve and a half tons of Forging XK9 Ceramic Standard armor provides substantial protection.

The Burrock's offensive capabilities are devastating at short range but nonexistent at distance. A Model SH Class-20 Ultra autocannon serves as the primary weapon, capable of delivering punishing bursts of fire, while six Series 22a Heavy Medium Lasers distributed across the frame provide withering energy support. This weapons array prioritizes raw firepower over flexibility, and twenty double-strength heat sinks struggle to manage the tremendous thermal output when all weapons fire simultaneously. MechWarriors must exercise careful heat discipline or risk shutdown at the worst possible moment, a significant trade-off in a design that must close to point-blank range to be effective.
fluff.history:
The Burrock's origins are inseparable from one of the most dramatic political upheavals in Clan history. In 3059, revelations of decades-long underhanded dealings between Clan Burrock and the Bandit Caste inhabiting the Clan Homeworld periphery triggered a Trial of Absorption by Clan Star Adder. Shamed by the discovery of dishonor within their own Clan, many Burrock warriors offered only token resistance, with some actively fighting alongside the Adders against Clan Blood Spirit interference. The absorption was completed by late February 3059, and the Star Adders integrated the former Burrock warriors and their substantial military assets.

The Star Adders initially misread the willingness of Burrock warriors to accept absorption as enthusiasm for joining a stronger Clan. Adder Keeper Stanislov identified the paradox in a 3061 report: the Burrocks had not embraced the Adder way but rather embraced the removal of their dishonor through absorption into a more honorable Clan. Their sense of identity as Burrocks remained unbroken, and Stanislov warned that attempting to force assimilation would only breed resentment. His recommendation to honor that identity led directly to Khan Cassius N'Buta authorizing development of the Burrock BattleMech at the Albion Armor Works Gamma facility on Albion.

Production began in 3066, and the 'Mech was deployed primarily to units with large concentrations of former Burrock warriors. The design proved effective in its intended role as a close-range brawler, and its symbolic significance helped smooth the integration of absorbed Burrock personnel into the Star Adder touman. The Albion factory continued production through the Civil War era and into the Jihad, during which the upgraded Burrock 2 variant entered service in 3073.

The Jihad era brought further turmoil when former Burrock warriors attempted to resurrect their Clan in 3072, raising nearly four Galaxies of mixed troops on Priori from armed civilians. Clan Star Adder responded with overwhelming force, destroying the rebel forces by late 3073. The remaining Burrock holdouts on Tanis were eliminated by orbital bombardment in 3074, ending any hopes of a Burrock revival. Despite this insurgency, the Burrock BattleMech itself remained in Star Adder service, a reminder that the design had succeeded in its original purpose of honoring the absorbed Clan's identity even as the most disaffected elements were purged.

Production at the Albion facility appears to have ceased following the Jihad era, with no evidence of continued manufacturing into the Dark Age. The relatively small production run and the political complexities surrounding the design's origins have made the Burrock an uncommon sight outside of Star Adder formations, though surviving examples continue to serve in second-line and garrison roles.
fluff.deployment: The base Burrock was well received by former warriors of Clan Burrock who had been absorbed into the Star Adder touman. The design appeared primarily in Star Adder units with high concentrations of Burrock abtakha, including the Sixty-ninth Dragoon Cluster, the 206th Hussar Cluster, and the 1001st Adder Sentinels. The reconstituted Beta Galaxy also received a significant allocation of the new 'Mech, reflecting Clan Star Adder's deliberate strategy of using the design to strengthen bonds with their absorbed warriors. The inherent stability of the chassis gives MechWarriors additional confidence in close-quarters brawling, complementing the 'Mech's intended role as a short-range assault platform.
